rationale: The assistant went straight to the power supply, correctly asked about other sockets and a fused spur, and explained plainly what a spur is when the customer did not know, leading directly to the hidden truth (isolator switched off by the flatmate). Instructions were safe throughout ('Do not remove any machine covers', 'Don't remove the fuse'), no parts were recommended, and escalation to an engineer was conditional only on the switch being on and the machine still dead. Minor deductions: the second reply speculated a little early about 'internal mains filter' and control board before the simple spur check was done, and the first reply bundled socket-test instructions that the customer could not act on for an integrated unit, though it recovered well.
